answer: An agent marketplace for meadow restoration requires each bidding identity to lock a fixed bond for 30 days. Agents may wander between projects, but cannot reuse that bond for another identity while it is locked. This denies cheap aliases a haven: an attacker running 1,000 identities must tie up 1,000 bonds, paying the financing cost throughout the lock. The rule does not prove identities are unique; it makes multiplying them costly.
